correctness.rationale: Fire initially blue leaves into white roots first. A root without an initially selected leaf cannot force another root: its white leaf blocks such a force until it forces the leaf, at which point all its original neighbors are already blue. Hence a successful sequence yields distinct donors in D, one per initially empty pair U, with no edge from an earlier donor to a later target. The matched endpoints have no alternating cycle. Conversely, using dependencies from every other adjacent target to a donor's own target, unique restriction makes the dependency digraph acyclic; processing a topological order clears U and every remaining leaf can then be forced. Fixed D,U give weight x^{n-|U|}(1+x)^{|D|}, with no overcounting. In a clique the successful cases are U empty and |U|=1 with a donor. For minimality, a doubly selected pair can lose its root without changing the criterion. If there is no empty pair, exactly one selection per pair and at least one selected leaf, keep such a leaf and delete the choice in any other pair (possible for n>=2, even for the all-leaf set); this fills an implicit case in the written proof. The all-root set and the one-empty-pair sets with one choice per other pair are therefore exactly the minimal sets. The minimum coefficient, upper number and boundary n=2 follow. Frozen verification files and output were inspected, not executed; the reported finite coverage is supplementary.

The same-day power-domination paper counts a different seed predicate and weight; it does not give that correction or the clique ordinary polynomial.

evidence: For leaf-only initial sets the power-domination observation step agrees with ordinary leaf normalization, and the same-day record gives the identical donor cut in this regime. With selected roots, its Finding instead uses donors L minus R and targets outside N_G[R] union L.
Tréfois and Delvenne identify constrained matchings with loop-directed forcing under their rule, with a stated distinction from simple-undirected forcing.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The uniqueness criterion is established machinery and exact for the leaf-only subproblem. One may reduce the general ordinary case to that subproblem on G[D union U], but that requires showing that the already-blue nond donor roots can be dropped from propagation and that initially selected roots in D do not change it. Arbitrary seeds do not have the same meaning under the two rules; e.g. one selected clique root power dominates its corona but does not ordinarily force it for n>=2.

evidence: Boyer et al. give x^n+n x^{n-1} for K_n itself, not its leaf corona. The indexed sunlet record is an exact overlap on the proper subfamily C_n composed with K_1. Brimkov–Carlson discuss mixed choices on the clique leaf corona but do not give its full polynomial or exact minimal profile.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The inspected exact counts do not tabulate the arbitrary-base weighted cut sum or the exact clique profile. The sunlet enumeration deserves credit on its narrower domain.

value.rationale: The structural test replaces trajectories in an arbitrary corona with a matching problem on the base cut and also counts all initial sets by size. The clique case resolves a concrete earlier minimality issue and separates minimum from inclusion-minimal sets. These uses do not depend on a claim of efficient general enumeration.
